faq.heading: Common questions before starting a website or landing page project

item1.question: What is the difference between a corporate website and a landing page?
item1.answer: A corporate website presents the brand, services, proof and a broader navigation structure. A landing page is more focused and built for a specific offer, campaign or conversion objective.

item2.question: Can a landing page also rank on Google?
item2.answer: Yes, as long as it has the right technical structure, search-intent-aligned content and a relevant enough offer. Not every landing page exists only for paid media.

item3.question: Do you deliver only design or also content strategy and SEO?
item3.answer: The scope includes architecture definition, business-oriented content, technical SEO, conversion copy and implementation. Design is only one part of the delivery.

item4.question: Can this solution already launch with lead capture integrated?
item4.answer: Yes. We can connect forms, n8n automation, CRM, email and qualification flows so the website already operates as a commercial channel from launch.

item5.question: How much does a professional website cost?
item5.answer: The investment depends on the scope: a focused campaign or diagnostic landing page starts at a lower cost, while a full corporate website with solution pages, technical SEO and integrations requires proportional investment. We recommend requesting a diagnosis so we can present a proposal aligned with your goals and budget.

item6.question: How long does it take to build a website or landing page?
item6.answer: A focused landing page can be delivered in 5 to 10 business days. A full corporate website with multiple pages, content architecture and integrations typically takes 3 to 6 weeks, depending on the number of pages and project complexity.

item7.question: What are Core Web Vitals and why do they affect my site's ranking?
item7.answer: Core Web Vitals are Google's performance metrics that assess load speed (LCP), interactivity (INP) and visual stability (CLS). Sites with good scores tend to have an organic ranking advantage. Every QuantumTech delivery is optimized to achieve PageSpeed 90+ and Core Web Vitals approval.

item8.question: Next.js or WordPress: which is the better choice for a business website?
item8.answer: It depends on the objective. WordPress is a solid choice for editorial content with frequent updates by non-technical teams. Next.js is the ideal choice when the project demands high performance, advanced technical SEO, external system integrations, multilingual structure and scalability without plugin limitations. For brands that need digital authority, conversion and continuous technical evolution, Next.js is our recommendation.

item9.question: What is GEO and why does my website need it in 2026?
item9.answer: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is the practice of optimizing content to appear as a cited source in AI-generated answers — Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Bing Copilot and ChatGPT Search. In 2026, a growing share of commercial searches results in synthetic responses where Google or AI lists agencies, services and solutions. Appearing in those citations requires specific technical structure: FAQPage, HowTo schema, AggregateRating, citeable prose and E-E-A-T signals. Every website delivered by QuantumTech already includes this foundational structure.

faq.heading: Common questions before implementing generative AI and agents

item1.question: What is an AI agent and how does it differ from a simple chatbot?
item1.answer: A simple chatbot follows a fixed flow of questions and answers. An LLM-powered AI agent understands natural language, accesses external tools (APIs, databases, email) and can execute multi-step actions autonomously. An agentic system goes further: it receives an objective and decides on its own which tools to use and in what sequence to achieve it.

item2.question: What is RAG and when should I use it?
item2.answer: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) connects an LLM to a proprietary document base so it answers accurately about your content — without retraining the model. Use RAG when your company has documents, manuals, contracts or knowledge bases that the model does not know by default. This ensures precise answers without hallucinations about your specific context.

item3.question: What is the difference between n8n automation and generative AI?
item3.answer: n8n is a flow orchestration tool that connects systems, APIs and triggers. Generative AI (LLMs) adds reasoning, natural language and semantic decision-making. The two work together: n8n orchestrates the flow (when to trigger, what to connect), the LLM processes and decides (classify, summarize, generate, respond). The combination eliminates brittle automations based on fixed rules.

item4.question: Does my company need GPT-4o, Claude or can I use smaller models?
item4.answer: It depends on the use case. For simple tasks (classification, extraction, summarization), smaller models like GPT-4o mini, Claude Haiku or Llama 3 have much lower cost with equivalent results. For complex reasoning or legal analysis, GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet are more appropriate. We always evaluate cost, latency and privacy to recommend the right model.

item5.question: Is company data secure when using LLMs?
item5.answer: Yes, with the correct architecture. We use RAG so proprietary data stays in your infrastructure and only relevant excerpts are sent to the model. We configure with no training data storage (OpenAI Enterprise, Claude API with zero data retention). For high sensitivity, we deploy local models (Llama, Mistral) that never leave your environment.

item6.question: How long does it take to implement an AI agent?
item6.answer: A basic support agent with RAG can be implemented in 2 to 4 weeks. n8n + LLM automations for internal processes generally take 1 to 3 weeks per flow. More complex agentic systems with multiple tools and integrations take 6 to 12 weeks depending on scope.

item7.question: What is Agentic AI and why is it different from a common assistant?
item7.answer: Agentic AI is an architecture where the LLM acts as an autonomous orchestrator: it receives an objective, plans the necessary steps, calls tools, evaluates intermediate results and adjusts the plan until the task is complete. Unlike an assistant that answers questions, an agentic system can search the web, query a database, send an email and update a CRM — all autonomously.

item8.question: Is it possible to integrate the agent with WhatsApp, internal systems and CRM?
item8.answer: Yes. We integrate via WhatsApp Business API (official), REST APIs from CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive), ERPs, databases and any system with an available API. n8n acts as integration orchestrator, connecting the agent to the tool ecosystem the company already uses without replacing what works.

item9.question: What is the real ROI of implementing AI in my company?
item9.answer: The ROI depends on the use case and operation volume, but AI automation projects in support, qualification and document processes typically return 3 to 6 times the investment in 12 months. The main factors: 30-70% reduction in support costs, 4-8 hours saved per employee per week on document tasks and the ability to handle more demand without growing the team. Our free technical diagnosis maps the processes with the highest return potential before any investment.

item10.question: How quickly does AI automation start paying for itself?
item10.answer: For support and lead qualification automations, the typical payback is 60 to 120 days. n8n + LLM flows for triage and data extraction generally pay back in 30 to 60 days. RAG systems over internal documents usually show visible return in under 30 days from the immediate reduction in time the team spends searching for information — before any other optimization.

portal.guideSubtitle: How the Quantum Technology platform works, step by step.
portal.guide1Body: Everything starts in the form on the main page. Describe your project — type, problem you want to solve, target audience, desired features, budget and timeline. Our AI analyzes the briefing and automatically calculates a complexity score, estimated hours and similar projects already delivered by the team.
portal.guide2Body: Based on the generated technical scope, the team prepares a detailed proposal with hours, costs and terms. You can review the proposal, leave comments on specific paragraphs or request an AI-assisted rewrite. When you agree, approve to move forward.
portal.guide3Body: In addition to briefings, you can create direct requests — for a new feature, bug fix, technical support or new project. Each request has a dedicated message channel for real-time communication with the team.
portal.guide4BodyStart: When the proposal is approved, a payment session is generated via Stripe. You can pay securely by credit or debit card. After confirmation, the order is automatically moved to
portal.guide4BodyEnd: and you receive a digital invoice available for download.
portal.guide5BodyStart: When the work is delivered, the order is marked as
portal.guide5BodyEnd: . At that point you can leave a 1 to 5 star rating with an optional comment. Feedback is used by the team to continuously improve the service.
portal.guideHelpText: Have a question? Use the message channel on your order or contact us directly.
